message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$8,912 total), which is within your mandate: AAPL only, buy-only, under the $10,000 per-order cap, well under the $20,000 daily cap, and priced essentially at the current market (last $222.70, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72). The case rests on Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 report (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024): quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, with full-year net sales of $391.0B (up from $383.3B), net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating income of $123.2B — noting the year's net income and EPS were depressed by a one-time $10.2B tax charge, so underlying profitability was stronger than the headline decline suggests. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, meaning expectations are moderate rather than euphoric, which supports a modest starter position rather than a large one. I made no transfers and left the remaining cash (~$41,000) and the existing 100 MSFT shares untouched.
